_about: What each event's flyer said, plus a short recap of how the night went (from the club's Facebook posts). Times are as printed on the flyer.

2012-spring.where: Trackside campsites, just past the quarter-mile mark
2012-spring.food: Relax with a cold drink and we'll cook dinner.
recap: The very first Top End Club. Rodney Smith, Tim Ridge, Jerry Bishop and James Larson set up in the trackside campsites just past the finish line and cooked dinner for whoever came by after the race.

2012-fall.food: Relax with a cold drink and we'll cook dinner.

2015-spring.where: Trackside campsites, just past the quarter-mile mark
2015-spring.food: Chicken stew and barbecue. Relax with a cold drink and we'll cook dinner.

2015-fall.where: Trackside campsites, just past the quarter-mile mark
recap: The first flyer with the club's oval emblem.

2016-spring.where: Trackside campsites, just past the quarter-mile mark
2016-spring.food: Dinner for everyone. 100% of all donations went to D.R.A.W. in honor of two fallen friends.
recap: The first night the club gave to D.R.A.W. Every dollar, $1,460 in all, went to D.R.A.W. in honor of Mark Lyle and Ronnie Davis, two friends of the club lost that spring.

2016-fall.where: Trackside in the Sportsman pits, just past the timing lights
2016-fall.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.
recap: The night raised $1,425, bringing the club's giving to $2,885.
A month later, D.R.A.W. named the Top End Club its 2016 Organization of the Year, presented in Dallas on October 15, 2016.

2017-spring.where: Trackside in the Sportsman pits, just past the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2017-spring.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.
recap: The first event under the club's new gold emblem, with the flyer carrying D.R.A.W.'s 2016 Organization of the Year badge.

2017-fall.where: Trackside in the Sportsman pits, just past the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2017-fall.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.

2018-spring.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2018-spring.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.
recap: A new home: sites 13 and 14 in the Sportsman pits, right ahead of the timing lights. It has been the club's spot ever since.

2018-fall.when: After the second round of pro racing
2018-fall.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2018-fall.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.
recap: Held on the Hurricane Michael weekend. The night raised $1,724, and the club's giving to D.R.A.W. passed $10,000.

2019-spring.when: After the second round of pro racing
2019-spring.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2019-spring.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.
recap: By the end of this event, the club's seven D.R.A.W. nights had raised $12,582, by Rosalee Noble's count.

2019-fall.when: After the second round of pro racing
2019-fall.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2019-fall.food: The club catered dinner for everyone.
recap: Live music joined dinner. The night raised about $2,560, for $15,142 given in all.
It was the last event before COVID-19 cancelled 2020.
A private event, open mainly to sponsors and invited teams and guests, as racing came back from COVID-19.
The night raised $2,500, given in honor of Phillip "Kilroy" Bishop.
Another private event, open mainly to sponsors and invited teams and guests.
The night raised $2,363, which took the club past its $20,000 goal for D.R.A.W.

2022-spring.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2022-spring.food: A food buffet: the club catered dinner and drinks for everyone, with several barbecue dishes and all the fixings.
recap: On the 4-Wide Nationals weekend, the night raised $3,510, a club record at the time, for $23,555 given in all.

2022-fall.when: After the final round of pro qualifying
2022-fall.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the timing displays
2022-fall.food: The club caters dinner for everyone. Help yourself: several barbecue dishes and a full spread of fixings.
recap: "See you at the top end." Jimmy Freeman played, and the night raised $2,665, for $26,220 given in all.

2023-spring.when: After the final round of pro qualifying
2023-spring.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the timing displays
2023-spring.food: The club caters dinner for everyone. Help yourself: several barbecue dishes and a full spread of fixings.
recap: The night raised $5,158, a new club record, for $31,378 given in all.

2023-fall.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the timing displays
2023-fall.food: Several barbecue dishes and a full spread of fixings. Bring your appetite and your wallet: it's all for D.R.A.W.

music.name: The Rockaholics
music.note: Presented by Jim & Flo Gottman and AllTech Sign Service

music.name: Sammy Eubanks
music.note: Known from the NHRA Camping World tour pit entertainment

recap: Three acts played: The Rockaholics, Jimmy Freeman and Sammy Eubanks. The night raised $4,400 ($4,398, rounded up with $2 from Tim Ridge), for $35,778 given in all.

2024-spring.where: Sportsman pits, directly ahead of the timing displays
2024-spring.food: Several barbecue dishes and a full spread of fixings, served from 6:00 to 6:30.

music.name: DJ
music.note: Presented by Jim & Flo Gottman and AllTech Sign Service

recap: The club set a goal of $40,000 given. The night raised $6,105, another record, for $41,883 in all.

2024-fall.where: Sportsman pits, ahead of the zMAX Dragway timing lights
2024-fall.food: Several barbecue dishes and a full arrangement of appetizer sides and fixings.

music.name: Live DJ
music.note: Presented by Jim Gottman and AllTech Sign Service

recap: Remembering Rosalee Noble. The night raised $8,880 in her memory, a record, and the club's all-time giving passed $50,000.

2025-spring.where: zMAX Sportsman pits, ahead of the timing lights
2025-spring.food: Several barbecue dishes and a full arrangement of appetizer sides and fixings.
2025-spring.auction: The club's first live auction, after dinner.
recap: The first live auction after dinner. The night raised $8,300, for $59,063 given in all.

2025-fall.where: Sportsman pits at zMAX Dragway, directly ahead of the timing lights
2025-fall.food: Several barbecue dishes and an assortment of appetizers, sides and other fixings.
2025-fall.auction: An open live auction after dinner, emceed by Jack Beckman and Jim Campbell.
recap: The final fall event, and a celebration of life for Rosalee Noble. Jack Beckman and Jim Campbell emceed the live auction.
It was the club's most successful night to date: about $29,350 raised, for $88,413 given in all.

2026-spring.food: A free buffet at 6:30: the club caters dinner for everyone, with many barbecued dishes and appetizers.
2026-spring.auction: The club's third live benefit auction, at 7:30. All money from the auction and other donations went to D.R.A.W.
recap: The only event of 2026, as the club moved to one big spring night a year. Admission to the club was free.
The night raised $11,592, including $910 from Paul Miller of the Oliver & Miller fuel altered team and $5 from Rodney's son, which took the club's all-time giving to D.R.A.W. past $100,000: $100,005.
